title: Supervised spectral analysis distinguishes colorectal precancerous lesions in a 100-person serum study
summary: A serum spectroscopy study analyzed 30 healthy controls,30 people with colorectal precancerous lesions and 40 with colorectal cancer. Supervised class-discrimination optimization after principal-component analysis distinguished these groups in five-fold cross-validation; the reported precancer-versus-other-groups AUC was 0.96. These are internal classification results from 100 participants, without an independent screening cohort or demonstrated clinical benefit. Spectral differences do not establish a molecular disease mechanism.
ai_technology: Optimal Class Discrimination and Compactness Optimization; support vector machine; k-nearest neighbors

evidence.tested: Five-fold cross-validation of spectra from 100 participants across three diagnostic groups; source reports precancer-versus-other-groups AUC 0.96. Multiple measurements per sample were averaged before analysis.
evidence.unknown: No external patient cohort, prospective screening validation or treatment-benefit study. Methods report averaging five spatial spectra per sample and five-fold cross-validation, but do not explicitly establish patient-grouped fold assignment or fold-local PCA and component selection; reported internal spectral classification is not established patient-level screening performance. Biochemical interpretations remain associations.
evidence.ai_role: After PCA preprocessing, supervised Optimal Class Discrimination and Compactness Optimization learned separation of diagnostic classes from labeled spectra. SVM and nearest-neighbor classifiers provided comparison models; PCA alone is not the enabling AI contribution.

source_review.scope: Exact primary article-front DOI/title/PMCID and date; full relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; fresh PubMed publication types and correction/retraction relationship metadata.
